blocks.x: Engineering standards & stack

items: Credentials that verify cryptographically without phoning home to a vendor.
Records anchored by hash so tampering is detectable — trust with a checksum.
Shared ledgers with known counterparties and governed writes — DLT where it earns its keep.
What must be tamper-evident goes on ledger; the bulk stays off it, linked and provable.

blocks.x: Operational telemetry
What we watch so you do not have to ask:

items: Up 95–99.4% automated at ingest on the first working slice; deeper scope moves it further
Settlement elapsed time measured end to end, with each hand-off timed separately.

blocks.x: Failure modes & the guards we ship
Failure modes we design against, with the guard shipped for each:

items: On-chain PII — guarded because personal data never touches the ledger; only salted hashes and pointers are anchored
Ledger worship: a chain only helps where counterparties dispute truth; workflows that already trust one database stay on one database; the guard is part of the first slice, not a hardening phase
Key fragility — root keys live in HSMs under dual control with ceremony logs; rotation is rehearsed, not documented
